statements.text: I believe AI has real potential to improve lives – but it also comes with real risks and shouldn’t involve giving Big Tech a blank check. AI should work for all of us, not just for the companies building it.
I also support commonsense AI safeguards to protect children interacting with chat bots and make sure the newest models don’t pose major risks to our cybersecurity.

We should know if massive layoffs or displacements are happening because of AI and corporations should have to give notice before replacing employees with AI. If this replacement happens, big tech and the companies that profit should be required to pay into a fund that helps retrain workers who lose their jobs to AI so workers don’t lose their livelihoods as our economy transitions into the AI age.

We are actively helping China to develop better AI capabilities because we don't have proper restraints on chips that are are sent there. So whatwe need to dois make sure we're not sending China the tools it needs to continue to advance in AI, while at the same timeputting up much needed guardrails
Right now, I don’t feel that there’s a coherent (AI regulation) strategy coming out of Congress, and part of the problem is Congress is really old and they don’t understand AI,
statements.venue: Commerce Lexington candidate forum, reported by Lexington Herald-Leader

statements.text: Congress needs to have aggressive regulation on AI development while keeping the U.S. globally competitive. Primarily, we need real child-safety measures, so our kids aren’t being harmed. [...] It’s crucial we have full transparency from AI developers when their AI bots hack another company or private database. We also need hardware measures so that AI research can continue without the risk that advanced AI bots can escape containment.
It’s important for national security that the United States does not let China surpass us in the AI race, but there are ways to do that safely without creating unnecessary risks.

The federal government needs to stand up for these communities and make sure AI data centers are not only respecting community input, but that if they do come in, rate payers don’t pay an extra cent and that water and fertile farmland is protected,
